properties.areaDesc: Blaine, OK; Caddo, OK; Canadian, OK; Grady, OK
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 14 at 10:17AM CDT until October 16 at 4:36AM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the
following rivers in Oklahoma...

Canadian River near Bridgeport affecting Blaine, Canadian, Caddo
and Grady Counties.

For the Upper Canadian River...including Bridgeport...Major flooding
is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Canadian River near Bridgeport.

* WHEN...Until late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Flooding affects croplands... pastures...
and oil wells near the river. Flood plain fields at higher
elevations away from the river may be cut off from easy access by
high water in side channels. Sand dredging operations are affected.
Upstream points in southern Blaine County may see flooding before
the areas near Bridgeport in northern Caddo County. Downstream
points in southwestern Canadian County are affected hours later.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 16.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 14.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 AM CDT Wednesday was 16.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.2 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late tomorrow
evening.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.3
feet on 05/26/2019.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1030 PM CDT.

properties.areaDesc: Canadian, OK; Cleveland, OK; Kingfisher, OK; Logan, OK; Oklahoma, OK
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 14 at 10:00AM CDT until October 14 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
FFWOUN

The National Weather Service in Norman has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Canadian County in central Oklahoma...
Northwestern Cleveland County in central Oklahoma...
Southeastern Kingfisher County in central Oklahoma...
Southwestern Logan County in central Oklahoma...
Oklahoma County in central Oklahoma...

* Until 100 PM CDT.

* At 1000 AM CDT, broadcast media reported thunderstorms producing
widespread flash flooding in the Oklahoma City metro. Between 3 and
6 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Broadcast media reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Oklahoma City, western Norman, Edmond, Moore, Midwest City, Del
City, El Reno, Guthrie, Newcastle, Yukon, Bethany, Mustang,
Choctaw, Warr Acres, The Village, Tuttle, Piedmont, Spencer,
Nichols Hills and Jones.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 1:00 PM CDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:00 PM CDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Norman has issued a Flood Advisory

For the Washita River...including Cheyenne, Clinton, Carnegie,
Anadarko, Chickasha, Alex, Lindsay, Pauls Valley, Dickson...elevated
river levels are forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1000 PM CDT.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Washita River near Clinton.

* WHEN...From this morning to Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Near bankfull conditions occur along the
Washita River... from areas near the mouth of Barnitz Creek... to
near Clinton in Custer County... and downstream to near the town of
Cloud Chief in Washita County. Flooding is limited to only bottom
lands where smaller streams enter the Washita River valley.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 16.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.3 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Action stage is 16.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
